itemListElement.name: Google Forms Right to Left: How to Make RTL Forms

@graph.name: How to flip Google Forms to right to left (language workaround)

step.name: Open Google Forms
step.text: Sign in to forms.google.com with the Google account you build forms with.

step.name: Open Google Account settings
step.text: Click your profile icon, then Manage your Google Account, then Personal info, then Language.

step.name: Add an RTL language
step.text: Add Arabic, Hebrew, Urdu, or Persian and set it as primary.

step.name: Refresh Google Forms
step.text: Reload forms.google.com. The editor and every form you open or create defaults to RTL.

@graph.description: Change your Google account's Forms language to an RTL language (Arabic, Hebrew, Urdu, Persian) to flip the form editor to right-to-left alignment.

@graph.name: How to make a native RTL form in Formester

step.name: Build your base form
step.text: Use the AI form builder or open an existing form.

step.name: Toggle Multilanguage on
step.text: Open Advanced settings and switch Multilanguage on.

step.name: Add an RTL language and translate
step.text: Click Add Language, pick Arabic, Hebrew, Urdu, or Persian, then click Translate with AI.

step.name: Preview and share
step.text: Hit Preview, test on mobile, then share by link, QR code, or one of the six embed modes.

@graph.description: Build a form once, add Arabic, Hebrew, Urdu, or Persian as a language, AI translates and aligns RTL.

mainEntity.name: Does Google Forms officially support right to left?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google has not shipped an RTL setting. The only workaround is to change your Google account's Forms language to an RTL language, which flips the form direction in your own editor and preview. Respondents on default-English Google accounts still see a left-to-right form.

mainEntity.name: What other form builders support RTL natively?

acceptedAnswer.text: Formester (toggle Multilanguage, pick an RTL language, AI translates and aligns), Fillout (per-form Right-to-left toggle), and Jotform (paste a custom CSS block) all support RTL. forms.app and Gravity Forms also offer RTL with setup beyond a single toggle.

mainEntity.name: How do I add a Hebrew or Arabic form to my website?

acceptedAnswer.text: Build the form in a native RTL builder (Formester, Fillout, or Jotform), then embed it. In Formester, click Share and pick from six embed modes (inline, popup, sidebar, side tab, popover, fullscreen). The form keeps its RTL alignment inside the iframe.

mainEntity.name: Can I have one form with both English and Arabic versions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in any builder with a multilanguage feature. Formester ships a language picker that lets respondents switch between English, Arabic, Hebrew, or any combination of 180+ languages. Google Forms does not have a native multilanguage feature.

mainEntity.name: Does the Google Forms language hack work for respondents?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The account-language setting is per-Google-account. Each respondent sees the form in their own account's language, not yours.

mainEntity.name: Which RTL languages does Formester support?

acceptedAnswer.text: Formester's AI translation covers 180+ languages including Arabic, Hebrew, Urdu, Persian (Farsi and Dari), Pashto, Sindhi, and Kurdish (Sorani). RTL alignment applies automatically when the language is RTL.

mainEntity.name: Will my form work on mobile in RTL?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in any builder with native RTL. Touch targets, submit button placement, and label alignment all stay correct at every breakpoint.

mainEntity.name: Can I use dir=rtl in HTML to make my own form RTL?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Set dir=rtl on the form element (or a parent) and pair it with the right lang attribute (ar, he, ur, fa). For mixed-direction content like Latin-script brand names inside an RTL body, wrap them in bdi tags.
